text:
Maya K: Quick sync — we need a straight answer on ordering for Optimize toolkit features. Customers keep asking for quant + batch + cache. How do we sequence for max impact vs effort?

Leo R: +1. Can we avoid a big monolith? prefer incremental.

Sam T: My gut: caching prefix KV first (low risk), then batching improvements, then quantization. But depends on metrics — batch helps throughput, quant helps cost per token.

Maya K: Agreed. Need RICE-style numbers though. I can draft a quick rubric: Reach = #customers impacted, Impact = cost/latency delta for typical workloads, Confidence = data quality, Effort = engineering weeks.

Jin Park: Draft RICE for three initiatives:
- Cache (prefix + KV): R:6 I:5 C:8 E:3 => score 240
- Batching (continuous + priority queues): R:7 I:6 C:6 E:6 => score 252
- Quantization (8-bit/4-bit support + eval): R:5 I:8 C:5 E:9 => score 200

Aisha S: Where are we getting Reach numbers? Is that internal customers + top 5 paying customers? we should weight enterprise requests heavier.

Maya K: For now use active tenants with >$5k/month usage as reach signal. We can refine.

Leo R: Notes: batching effort might be underestimated. Runtime changes + kernel selection + QA. Might be closer to 10w if we include cross-region routing.

Sam T: True. If batching is 10w then score drops. Also batching may require datastore changes for request shaping.

Maya K: Can we separate batching into MVP (smarter micro-batching, non-invasive) vs v2 (priority queues + region-aware)?

Jin Park: Yes:
- Batching MVP: R:7 I:5 C:7 E:4 => 245
- Batching v2: R:7 I:7 C:5 E:8 => 245
(rough math, keeps parity)

ProductBot: Deploy-checklist created for "opt-toolkit/priority" — auto-assign to eng-runtime.

Aisha S: Customers asking specifically for quantization because of cost. One enterprise (FinCo) asked for 4-bit for cheaper embeddings. They will pilot if we ship within Q2.

Maya K: That’s an important demand signal. FinCo counts as high-reach. Add +2 to Reach for enterprise pilots.

Leo R: Another constraint: quantization requires eval gating and hallucination regressions checks. We need an evaluation harness and roll-back plan. Effort includes eval work.

Sam T: Cache MVP is attractive: relatively low effort, immediate p95 latency wins on session-heavy workloads. We can ship and measure token savings via instrumentation.

Maya K: Proposed launch criteria per initiative:
- Cache MVP: p95 latency improvement >=10% on chat workloads OR token cost reduction >=5% for top 10 customers; instrumentation in prod; canary to 5% traffic; docs and SDK hooks.
- Batching MVP: throughput improvement >=20% on steady loads; no >5% p95 regressions; fallbacks when overloaded; canary ramp plan.
- Quantization (pilot): embeddings MSE within delta threshold vs baseline; quality evals on NLU prompts; performance and cost benchmarks; pilot with FinCo.

Jin Park: Also include rollback triggers: any customer-reported quality regression >3 incidents/week or automated eval drift >threshold -> auto rollback.

Aisha S: From sales: if we promise FinCo pilot in Q2 we need a clear timeline. They will sign an NDA and give us datasets.

Maya K: Timeline suggestion: Cache MVP 6w, Batching MVP 8w (parallel infra work), Quant pilot 10-12w (eval heavy). Prioritize Cache first, but start quant eval in parallel (small spike) because of enterprise ask.

Leo R: Parallel spikes make sense. We can allocate 1 eng to quant investigation (4w spike) while 2 squads do cache + batching MVP.

Sam T: Risk matrix:
- Cache: low risk, medium impact, quick wins.
- Batching: medium risk, high infra effort, long lead.
- Quant: high impact on cost, high risk on quality, long eval.

Maya K: Decision check: do we sequence Cache -> Batching MVP -> Quant pilot, with a parallel quant spike now?

Jin Park: I support. Also plan experiment metrics: cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency, eval-score delta per prompt set, and deployment failure rate.

Aisha S: Sales ok with that sequencing if we lock FinCo pilot for quant and keep them in the loop.

ProductBot: Reminder: add roadmap ticket to "product/optimize-toolkit" and tag stakeholders.

Maya K: I'll write PRD for Cache MVP today with the launch criteria and metrics. Assigning owners: Cache -> Jin (eng-runtime), Batching MVP -> Sam (eng-platform), Quant spike -> Leo (eng-ml).

Leo R: I'll start quant eval matrix: baseline runs, 8-bit LLMs, 4-bit runs, check embedding MSE and 1k-shot sampling consistency. Will post results in this thread.

Sam T: I'll sketch batching MVP design (micro-batching + backpressure hooks) and list infra risks.

Jin Park: Will draft cache implementation plan and SDK hooks. Also add a small config for per-tenant TTL.

Maya K: Great. Final ask: everyone add R/I/E numbers in comments in GitHub issue I just created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/product/issues/1120 and we'll lock prioritization by EOD Friday. :thumbsup: 

Leo R: ack.

Sam T: ack.

Aisha S: ack.

Jin Park: ack.
